concepts.title: Mirror Formula
concepts.definition: A mathematical relation connecting the object distance, image distance, and focal length for any spherical mirror.
concepts.key_idea: Relates distances of object and image from the pole to the mirror's focal length.
question_patterns: calculate the image distance
find the position of the image
at what distance should the screen be placed
determine where the image is formed
calculate mirror formula for the given values

solution_steps.action: Calculate the reciprocal of the focal length
Calculate the reciprocal of the object distance
Find the reciprocal of the image distance

concepts.title: Magnification of Mirrors
concepts.definition: The ratio of the image's height to the object's height, which also relates to the distances from the mirror.
concepts.key_idea: Indicates how much larger or smaller the image is compared to the object.
question_patterns: find the magnification
calculate the size of the image
what is the height of the image
determine the nature and size of the image
what is the result in this magnification of mirrors problem

solution_steps.explain: A negative m indicates an inverted real image while a positive m indicates an erect virtual image; the absolute value tells how much larger or smaller the image is than the object.

concepts.title: Lens Formula
concepts.definition: A mathematical expression relating the object distance, image distance, and focal length for spherical lenses.
concepts.key_idea: Determines image position for lenses using the Cartesian sign convention.
question_patterns: find the image distance for the lens
calculate where the image is formed
at what distance should the object be placed
determine the focal length of the lens
work out the value using lens formula

solution_steps.explain: Assign positive sign for distances measured in the direction of incident light and negative for opposite directions to determine whether the image is real (positive v) or virtual (negative v).

concepts.title: Power of a Lens
concepts.definition: How strongly a lens bends light toward or away from its axis, measured as one divided by the focal length expressed in metres.
concepts.key_idea: Power is measured in dioptres (D) when focal length is in meters.
question_patterns: calculate the power of the lens
find the focal length from power
what is the power of a lens with given focal length
determine the dioptre value
what is the result in this power of a lens problem

solution_steps.explain: P = 1 / f (where f is in meters)

solution_steps.action: convert focal length to meters if needed
solution_steps.explain: Ensure the focal length is expressed in metres before computing power, since the dioptre unit requires metres as the input unit.
A positive power indicates a converging (convex) lens while a negative power indicates a diverging (concave) lens.
